title: Ulyana and the Inheritance
premise: Jude Reyes, a concierge at the Marlowe Grand who has spent a decade reading guests like room keys, becomes obsessed with a missing guest, Ulyana Petrova, after her abandoned diary keeps being written in—entries dated weeks past her disappearance, describing Jude himself. The diary leads him to believe Ulyana staged her death to escape the men she was set to testify against, and that the only witness who can convict them is someone the police and the press have declared dead. As the trial date closes in, Jude must track her through the hotel's hidden economy of bribes, aliases, and night-shift confidences, all while the diary's author grows more knowing—and more threatening. In the end Jude finds Ulyana alive but broken by what survival cost her, and together they choose justice outside the law: exposing the conspirators publicly rather than trusting a courtroom they know is bought.
about_author: Ines Okafor is a former night auditor for a chain of luxury hotels who spent years collecting the strange true stories of the small hours. She writes mysteries about invisible people—the staff, the witnesses, the ones everyone swears are dead.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Checked Out Sideways
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A routine shift ends with police questioning: Room 1104's occupant, Ulyana Petrova, vanished three weeks ago, leaving luggage and a locked drawer. Jude realizes he remembers her perfectly—she tipped too precisely, watched the elevators too long. Emotional beat: unease; the professional observer realizes he was observed back.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Asked to inventory the room, Jude finds the diary hidden in the minibar panel. The last entry is dated nine days after Ulyana disappeared—and it describes him, by name, folding towels. Emotional beat: vertigo; the mystery turns personal and impossible.

chapters.title: What the Night Staff Knows
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He quietly canvases the overnight crew: a housekeeper recalls a woman crying in the service stairwell; a valet remembers a black sedan with government plates. His manager warns him off. Emotional beat: solidarity of the invisible workers versus institutional silence.

chapters.title: The Trial Date
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. News coverage reveals Ulyana was the star witness against the Voss shipping family in a trafficking trial starting in six weeks—with no witness, the case may collapse. The diary's post-disappearance entries grow more urgent. Emotional beat: stakes crystallize; Jude decides to keep reading.

chapters.title: Room 1104, Revisited
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Breaking into the sealed room, he finds scratch marks under the wallpaper spelling a name: MIRA. Someone else lived hidden here, or still does. He hears footsteps and flees through the laundry chute. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Mira of the Mezzanine
chapters.summary: Mira's POV (introduced). A banquet captain who has survived the Voss orbit before, Mira admits she sheltered Ulyana but claims she's dead: 'I saw the body.' Her terror is real, and so is a flicker of doubt. Emotional beat: grief braided with suspicion.

chapters.title: The Diary Writes Back
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A new entry appears in the diary—which never left his locker—thanking him for finding Mira, and warning him to stop. Emotional beat: violation and dread; the hunter realizes he is bait.

chapters.title: Voss Water
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A charming 'hotel consultant' named Anselm Voss checks in, comping Jude's debts and asking friendly questions about 1104. Jude plays dumb while noticing Voss's bodyguard wears a stairwell-mud-stained boot. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal—bribes as soft violence.

chapters.title: Dead Women Don't Tip
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Following the diary's odd financial details, Jude traces cash withdrawals made in Ulyana's name after her death—at a bank branch whose camera caught a figure in a hotel uniform coat. Emotional beat: hope igniting; the dead witness is moving money.

chapters.title: The Body That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Flashback chapter: how Mira helped fake Ulyana's death with an unclaimed corpse from the morgue where her sister worked—and why she now believes the plan curdled into something worse. Emotional beat: guilt; good intentions priced in blood.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude confronts the lead detective, who privately admits the case is dying and the witness list is leaking. He half-believes Jude's diary theory—or wants to use him. Emotional beat: justice inside the law shown as compromised machinery.

chapters.title: Locker 9
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A bus station locker key taped inside the diary yields Ulyana's real testimony recordings—and a photo of Mira's sister, alive, held as leverage. Emotional beat: fury; the found-family thread tightens around shared danger.

chapters.title: Anselm's Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Voss offers Jude a job, a flat, and a future if he hands over 'any papers' from 1104. Jude accepts a drink, plants a lie about the diary's location, and walks out shaking. Emotional beat: temptation and self-loathing; survival has a menu of prices.

chapters.title: The Night Shift Confession
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, rotating short sections among doorman, housekeeper, valet. Each confesses a piece of what they saw and hid, stitched together by Jude listening. Emotional beat: warmth; the hotel's invisible people become a conspiracy of care.

chapters.title: Where the Dead Go Swimming
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Decoding diary references to a shuttered rooftop pool, Jude finds signs someone has been living there—canned food, a sleeping bag, a wall of clippings about the trial. Emotional beat: closeness; he is one floor above the truth.

chapters.title: Ulyana
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She reveals herself: not dead, not free—trapped between Voss's men and a prosecution that will burn her. She wrote the later diary entries herself, testing whether Jude could be trusted. Emotional beat: raw, exhausted humanity; the myth becomes a person.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Jude's POVs alternating. She explains the bargain she fled: testify and her protectors die, run and the trial dies. Jude proposes a third path—make the evidence public so killing her becomes pointless. Emotional beat: fragile alliance; two survivors choosing each other.

chapters.title: What Voss Bought
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Using concierge access, Jude documents Voss's network: judges' clerks, a detective, the morgue. Mira risks everything to copy the ledger. They learn the trial will be torpedoed from within in three days. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the law itself is on the take.

chapters.title: Check-Out Time
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Voss corners Jude in the penthouse, having traced the lie. Jude stalls with hospitality patter while Ulyana, via the service corridors, triggers the fire system and the dead woman walks through a lobby full of cameras. Emotional beat: high-wire tension turning triumphant.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Swears Is Dead
chapters.summary: Climax. Ulyana's testimony streams live as Voss's men close in; the staff lock down the service routes, buying minutes with linen carts and master keys. The recordings go everywhere before anyone can stop them. Emotional beat: catharsis; justice seized outside the law because the law was sold.

chapters.title: Depositions
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Fallout: arrests, a disgraced detective testifying, Voss's empire cracking. Ulyana, in protective custody, sends Jude the diary's final page—an entry written in her own hand, dated today, addressed to him. Emotional beat: bittersweet vindication; costs tallied honestly.

chapters.title: The Long Shift
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, epilogue. Months later, Jude still works the desk, now training a nervous new hire to notice everything. Ulyana visits incognito; Mira runs the mezzanine; the found family holds its shape. Last line mirrors the first diary entry—but this time it's Jude writing. Emotional beat: quiet peace earned, vigilance kept.
